newsitem.title: USA: SEC charges Mass. investment firm with fraud.
newsitem.headline: SEC charges Mass. investment firm with fraud.

text.p: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on Monday filed a complaint against a Massachusetts investment company and its owners, charging they defrauded more than 150 clients.

Hyannis Trading Advisors Inc of Osterville, Massachusetts, is accused of losing $6.0 million of the $7.5 million in investments the firm attracted through a program created to trade S&P 100 Index options, the SEC said.

The SEC alleges that between October and December 1992, the firm, its principal Jeremiah Hegarty and his brother Michael Hegarty fraudulently solicited investors with an advertisement and subsequently lost most of their clients' money.

According to SEC spokesman Grant Ward, Hegarty entered a contest in options trading and did quite well. On the basis of the competition results, he took out an advertisement in Investors Business Daily and quickly attracted clients, Ward told Reuters in an interview.

"The problems arose when he verbally told these clients that the risk features would protect them and keep their losses to a minimum. He also told them he would not trade their investments very often, no more than 40 or 50 times a year," Ward said. In the last three months of 1992, "he traded well in excess of that number," Ward said.

Ward said Hegarty had acquired so many clients, in California, New York and Massachusetts and elsewhere, "that instead of hiring another person to keep track of their positions, he and Michael just traded blind," Ward said.
The SEC said the firm, which remains in business and Jeremiah Hegarty, who remains a licensed investment adviser, lost about 80 percent the funds under management.
The SEC is seeking permanent injunctions, disgorgement and civil penalties from the three defendants.

Hegarty's lawyer, Joseph Carmichael, said in a telephone interview that his client "is a very successful adviser with a good track record. These people lost money due to the vagaries of the stock market...He deeply regrets that."
